title: Father's death deepens tragedy
subtitle: Even though police had removed the yellow tape cordoning off a south Oshawa townhouse, and the blood-soaked apartment had been cleaned up, the victims of a horrendous crime committed there a week ago continue to die.
article: Even though police had removed the yellow tape cordoning off a south Oshawa townhouse, and the blood-soaked apartment had been cleaned up, the victims of a horrendous crime committed there a week ago continue to die.
Instead of returning home today, Rick Kelly joined his wife, Leslie, and their 3-year-old son Nathan as the latest victim to die from stab wounds inflicted by 47-year-old Gino Petralia last Saturday.
Kelly, who was apparently stabbed in the back of the head during the attack at a birthday party for his 11-year-old son Brandon, died in hospital early yesterday morning.

"They spent 55 minutes trying to revive him and his heart started five more times, but it just gave out," said a relative, who declined to give his name. "It was a blood clot to the main artery that leads to his heart."
An autopsy is planned for today, he said.
Leslie Kelly died of multiple stab wounds the night of the attack. Police later fatally shot Petralia, who had a violent history.

Everyone, including police, expected Rick to recover. He was supposed to be home to spend Christmas with his two children - Brandon and 5-year-old Riley,who is recovering from stab wounds in hospital - and his half-brother, Steven. The Kellys received custody of Steven after his mother, who was also Rick's mother, died in August.
From his hospital bed, Rick had called and messaged friends on Facebook to tell them how excited he was to see his sons, a close family friend said.

"His boys were always at the front of his mind. ...We talked about what the kids wanted for Christmas. I got this big list and I promised him I would make sure they got cared for," said the woman, declining to give her name. "He was looking forward to putting this all behind him and being strong for his boys. Then he took a turn for the worse." The neighbourhood was frigid and desolate yesterday. A man delivering Oshawa This Week said it was "eerie delivering after dark" there. Other neighbours said they weren't going out much. And friend of the family, Jasmine Short, said people are locking their doors again.
"Nobody wants to leave their doors open. Even when my husband is home, I keep them locked," said Short.
She said Leslie, Nathan, and Riley used to come over and play with her large black cat, Mr. Big. Now she wondered who would care for the surviving boys. "It's a shame. So close to Christmas."
Many in the neighbourhood refused to talk about the deepening tragedy, shaking their heads sadly.
A neighbour and close friend who did not want to be named stood in her apartment door with a dog. She said she heard about Rick's death early yesterday.
"He was going to be released (today)," she said. "I was at his mother's funeral. It was hard on the kids, but they all seemed like one big, happy family."
The Special Investigations Unit is still probing Petralia's shooting.
